**Title: Germany Surrenders Unconditionally - End of the Second World War**

Germany's surrender, which ended the 6-year war against Hitler's Germany, was signed in Reims on Friday, 8 May 1945, in the early morning. The German General Schnabel and several other high-ranking German officials were present. The surrender was signed between the German and the allies at midnight by General Keitel.

After 9 P.M., after considerable discussion, the German generals accepted the conditions as set by the allied powers, and at 11.42 P.M. the actual signing took place. Keitel signed the German surrender by order of the German supreme commander, Dönitz. The document of surrender in English and Russian was handed to the British staff.

Germany has surrendered unconditionally. All German ships will be interned in their present harbours. The German navy is to be disarmed, with the exception of certain small craft.

The German government must issue orders for all air, land, and naval forces to stop fighting at once; German forces must lay down their arms by 8 o'clock in the morning, German time, on Sunday the 8th of May 1945, and will at that time cease all active operations in the east, west, south, and north, with the exception of a fighting between partisans.

All German forces must also remain in their then present positions unless given orders to move by the allied commanders.

All arms, materiel, and property of the German armed forces will be subject to control by the allies. German forces will, at the direction of the supreme allied commanders, move rearwards as required by the allied forces.

The armed forces of Germany will be disarmed gradually and will not be allowed to leave their present area except for the carrying out of orders by the allies. All weapons will be collected and all ammunition burned if the proper facilities are not available for dumping.

In addition, the German government will issue an immediate order to all German military and civilian agencies to co-operate in the immediate demobilization of the German armed forces and to submit to the authority of the allied forces.

Hitler's rule ended, as the remnants of his government, led by Dönitz, capitulated before the Western and Eastern allies at once.
